claim.pdf_says: [measured left ink columns at 300 dpi] 'I-O-CONTROL.' / 'DATA DIVISION.' / 'FD  STCK-FILE.' all begin at x=455; 'SELECT CHNG-FILE', the two preceding comment lines '*> will be locked by this program until a commit or' / '*> rollback.', and 'APPLY COMMIT ON STCK-FILE CHNG-FILE UPDATE-COUNT.' all begin at x=563 - exactly four character cells (1 cell = 26.7 px) further right.
claim.markdown_says:
*> will be locked by this program until a commit or
        *> rollback.

        SELECT CHNG-FILE
            ASSIGN TO "CHANGE"
...
        I-O-CONTROL.
            APPLY COMMIT ON STCK-FILE CHNG-FILE UPDATE-COUNT.
claim.why_it_matters: In the markdown, 'SELECT CHNG-FILE' and its two preceding comment lines sit at 8 spaces - the SAME column as 'I-O-CONTROL.', 'DATA DIVISION.' and 'FD  STCK-FILE.' - whereas the PDF indents them four columns further in. The example illustrates COBOL reference format, where paragraph headers (FILE-CONTROL., I-O-CONTROL.) stand in Area A and their clauses (SELECT ...) in Area B; flattening the two to one column destroys that distinction. It is also internally inconsistent with the same program's first page: page 1051 correctly renders 'FILE-CONTROL.' at 8 spaces and 'SELECT STCK-FILE' at 12, so the identical construct is indented two different ways across the page break, and the comment block that starts on p1051 at 12 spaces resumes on p1052 at 8.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by pixel measurement of the 300-dpi render, not by eyeballing. Per-text-line left-ink columns on spec_p1052.png: 'I-O-CONTROL.' x=456, 'DATA DIVISION.' x=455, 'FILE SECTION.' x=455, 'FD  STCK-FILE.' x=455, '01  STCK-REC.' x=456 - i.e. one common base column. Against that: '*> will be locked by this program until a commit or' x=563, '*> rollback.' x=564, 'SELECT CHNG-FILE' x=562, 'APPLY COMMIT ON STCK-FILE CHNG-FILE UPDATE-COUNT.' x=559. Character pitch measured from within-line glyph clusters (e.g. 'ASSIGN TO "CHANGE"': A@640 -> O@854 over 8 cells; '03  STCK-KEY': 0@563 -> S@669 over 4 cells) is 26.7 px/cell. Correcting for per-glyph left side bearing (calibrated in-line: S ink sits 2.3 px right of A ink, D ink 2.7 px right of A ink, for the same cell), the base column and the SELECT column are separated by 107 px = exactly 4.00 cells. The claim's numbers are therefore accurate; the APPLY line's x=559 vs the quoted 563 is purely the 'A' glyph's smaller left bearing, same cell. The markdown (verified with explicit leading-space counts) puts '*> will be locked...', '*> rollback.' and 'SELECT CHNG-FILE' at 8 spaces - identical to 'I-O-CONTROL.', 'DATA DIVISION.', 'FILE SECTION.', 'FD  STCK-FILE.' - so the 4-column separation the PDF prints is gone. The text itself is complete and correctly ordered, so this is not a lost-content or reflow issue; but in a COBOL source listing inside the COBOL standard, column position is content: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 reference format admits only division/section/paragraph headers, level indicators and 01/77 level-numbers in Area A (cols 8-11), and a SELECT clause is body of the FILE-CONTROL paragraph and must start in Area B (col 12+). As transcribed, page 1052's example is not valid reference format, while the PDF's is. The claimed cross-page inconsistency also verifies both ways: markdown p1051 has 'FILE-CONTROL.' at 8 and 'SELECT STCK-FILE' at 12, and its comment block ('*> ... since once read they') at 12, while the continuation of that same sentence ('*> will be locked by this program until a commit or') resumes on p1052 at 8; and in the PDF the two pages agree - p1051 base col x=523 with SELECT/comments at x=631/632 (+4 cells), p1052 base x=455 with SELECT/comments at x=562/563 (+4 cells). Nothing here is page-break furniture, wrapping or hyphenation: the PDF prints an unambiguous, consistent 4-cell Area A / Area B step that the markdown collapsed to zero on this page only.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with one refinement and one addition. Refinement: the shift is not confined to 'SELECT CHNG-FILE' and the two comment lines - the whole SELECT CHNG-FILE block moved left. In the PDF the subordinate clauses ('ASSIGN TO "CHANGE"', 'ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL', 'ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL', 'FILE STATUS IS CHNG-FILE-STATUS', 'SHARING WITH ALL OTHER.') sit at x=640-643 = base+7 cells (3 cells right of SELECT; measured S-to-S, 'SHARING' @643 minus 'SELECT' @562 = 81 px = 3.03 cells, and identically on p1051: 711-631 = 80 px). The markdown renders them at 12 spaces = base+4. So relative to the base column the markdown moves the comment lines and SELECT by -4 and the clauses by -3. Addition: the -3 on the clauses is itself harmless - the markdown normalizes the PDF's 3-space sub-indent to 4 on BOTH pages (p1051 md has SELECT at 12 and clauses at 16, i.e. base+4/base+8 vs the PDF's base+4/base+7), so it is a consistent, meaning-preserving normalization. The only meaning-bearing defect is the one the claim names: on page 1052 alone, the two continuation comment lines and 'SELECT CHNG-FILE' lost their 4-column Area B indent and now start in Area A, in the same column as 'I-O-CONTROL.', 'DATA DIVISION.', 'FILE SECTION.' and 'FD  STCK-FILE.'. Fix: indent markdown lines 7, 8 and 10 of the page-1052 fence from 8 to 12 spaces, and lines 11-15 from 12 to 16, matching the page-1051 rendering of the identical construct.
